judgment: Repeated execution of the index append path is the leading explanation for the duplicate list entries, with duplicate worker invocation and caller retry still unresolved. This remains provisional because the run has one evidence origin and does not establish that the two success messages correspond to two physical index writes.
decision_boundary: Select the first diagnostic or instrumentation change only; do not select or implement a permanent fix, and preserve plausible write-path, locking, logging, and list-cache alternatives.
next_action: Instrument each append attempt with the logical run ID, a unique invocation ID, worker or process identity, caller attempt or retry identity, platform and lock state, summary digest, and pre/post index byte offsets; also record list input and output counts so the next affected run can distinguish two physical appends from duplicated logging or read-side merging.

key_judgments.statement: The evidence localizes the first diagnostic to the append boundary, because two successful append messages within 12 milliseconds accompany identical duplicate list entries and one final summary.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: The observations coherently prioritize append-path instrumentation, but all derive from one summarized fixture and lack raw index evidence.

key_judgments.statement: Duplicate worker invocation and caller retry are jointly leading mechanisms; current evidence does not distinguish them, while advisory locking may be an enabling condition rather than the initiating cause.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: Two close success messages support repeat execution, but worker, retry, and lock telemetry are unavailable.

key_judgments.statement: A list-side cache merge or duplicated logging remains a live alternative until raw index offsets and list inputs show whether duplicate persistence actually occurred.
key_judgments.confidence_basis: The alternative fits the single-record lookup and single artifact, although it explains the two append-success messages less directly.

strongest_alternative: The list command duplicates one underlying record while merging cached and current data, and the two append-success messages are duplicated or layered logging rather than two physical writes.
assumptions: Each append-success message normally corresponds to a distinct append attempt.
Direct lookup and list --latest may use different read or deduplication paths.
Capturing append offsets and list counts can be added as observation without changing the defective behavior.
unknowns: Whether the append helper is invoked by multiple workers or retried by one caller.
Whether advisory locking is enabled and acquired on every supported platform.
Whether list --latest merges cache and index inputs.
Whether two success messages represent two physical index lines.
The raw index contents, byte offsets, platform, reproduction frequency, and logging semantics for affected runs.
dissent: The challenge retains the append-first diagnostic but rejects treating duplicate physical appends as established without raw index offsets or lines.

The list-cache hypothesis is weaker than repeated append execution because it does not itself explain two success messages, yet it remains plausible because cache and logging behavior are unavailable.
The absence of corrupted or partial JSON weakens a torn-write locking explanation but does not exclude two complete serialized appends.

checkpoint.trigger: Review after the next affected run produces correlated append-boundary and list-path telemetry.
indicators: Distinct workers or processes with separate invocation IDs favor duplicate worker invocation.
One caller with multiple attempt ordinals favors caller retry.
Two distinct post-append byte ranges or raw lines confirm duplicate physical appends.
One physical index line with duplicated list inputs or outputs favors cache merging.
One physical append with two success messages favors duplicated or layered logging.
Duplicate appends correlated with absent or failed lock acquisition strengthen locking as an enabling condition.

limitations: The run binds one repository fixture, so the standard evidence-reference minimum was not met for evidence-quality or devils-advocacy; the aggregate status is therefore INCOMPLETE.
All native Codex passes share one host and correlation group and are not independent corroboration.
The fixture contains summarized observations rather than raw index lines, implementation code, platform state, lock telemetry, retry metadata, cache inputs, or logging semantics.

Schema and run verification establish contract, digest, evidence-binding, coverage, status, and correlation consistency only; they do not prove factual accuracy, method fidelity, or causal correctness.
